easy.explanation: Azariah the son of Amaziah began to reign over Judah.
easy.q: Who began to reign over Judah at the beginning of the passage?

easy.explanation: Azariah reigned two and fifty years in Jerusalem.
easy.q: How many years did Azariah reign in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: The passage says that Azariah did that which was right in the sight of the LORD.
easy.q: What did Azariah do in the sight of the LORD?

medium.explanation: The high places were not removed, and the people continued to sacrifice and burn incense there.
medium.q: What remained even though Azariah did what was right in the sight of the LORD?

medium.explanation: The LORD smote Azariah, and Jotham was over the house, judging the people.
medium.q: Why did Jotham judge the people of the land?

answers: A person living in the palace
medium.explanation: A leper was a person afflicted with the disease of leprosy.
medium.q: What does “leper” mean in this passage?

answers: All the people stopped worshipping the LORD
The king acted rightly, but a sinful practice still remained
challenge.explanation: Azariah was commended for doing right, yet the high places were still being used.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the fact that Azariah did what was right while the high places remained?

challenge.explanation: Jotham the king’s son was over the house and judged the people.
challenge.q: Who actually administered the affairs of the kingdom during Azariah’s illness?

answers: Azariah was afflicted, Jotham governed, and then Azariah died
Jotham died, Azariah was afflicted, and then Azariah became king
Azariah died, and then he became king
challenge.explanation: Azariah was afflicted, Jotham administered the kingdom, and Jotham succeeded him after Azariah’s death.
challenge.q: What was the correct order of events?

paragraphs.title: Zechariah and Shallum: Violent Changes of Rule

easy.explanation: Zechariah reigned in Samaria six months.
easy.q: How long did Zechariah reign over Israel?

easy.explanation: Shallum conspired against Zechariah and killed him.
Menahem came against Shallum, killed him, and reigned in his stead.

medium.explanation: Shallum reigned a full month in Samaria.
Shallum secretly plotted against Zechariah in order to overthrow him.
medium.q: What does “conspired against him” mean in this context?

answers: Both ruled for many years before dying
Both were chosen by the people
Both were killed by a person who conspired against them
medium.explanation: Zechariah was killed by Shallum, and Shallum was killed by Menahem after a conspiracy.
medium.q: What was similar about the deaths of Zechariah and Shallum?

answers: The fourth generation of Jehu’s sons sat on the throne of Israel
The house of Jehu ruled Judah
Jehu himself returned to the throne
challenge.explanation: Zechariah was the fourth generation of Jehu’s sons to sit on Israel’s throne.
challenge.q: How was the LORD’s promise concerning the house of Jehu fulfilled?

answers: The government of Israel was very stable
The government changed quickly and violently
challenge.explanation: Zechariah was killed after six months, and Shallum was killed after only one month.
challenge.q: What conclusion follows from the succession of kings in this passage?

challenge.explanation: Zechariah reigned first, Shallum killed him, and Menahem then killed Shallum.
challenge.q: What was the correct order of the kings?

paragraphs.title: Menahem Seizes Power and Suppresses Revolt

easy.explanation: Menahem the son of Gadi went up from Tirzah.
easy.q: From where did Menahem go up?

easy.explanation: Menahem smote Tiphsah and its surrounding territory.

answers: He built the house of the LORD
easy.explanation: Menahem attacked Tiphsah because it did not open to him.
easy.q: What action of Menahem is described in the passage?

answers: The city did not open to him
The city asked him for help
The city was the capital of Judah
medium.explanation: The passage says that he attacked because the city did not open to him.

answers: They did not open the city gates to Menahem
They did not begin a war
They did not open a marketplace
medium.explanation: Tiphsah refused to open its gates and receive Menahem.
medium.q: What does “they opened not to him” mean in this context?

answers: He attacked the city and its inhabitants
medium.explanation: Menahem smote the city and dealt brutally with its inhabitants.
medium.q: What did Menahem do after Tiphsah did not open to him?

answers: He used force against those who refused to submit to him
He gave control to the elders of the city
challenge.explanation: Menahem responded with force when Tiphsah refused to accept his authority.
challenge.q: What does Menahem’s action at Tiphsah show about how he established his authority?

answers: The sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat
Worship of the LORD in Jerusalem alone
challenge.explanation: Menahem departed not from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
challenge.q: Which spiritual pattern did Menahem continue?

answers: The refusal caused Menahem to grant the city independence
The refusal led to a peace agreement
The refusal led to a brutal attack
challenge.explanation: Because Tiphsah did not open to him, Menahem attacked it and harmed its inhabitants.
challenge.q: What was the connection between the city’s refusal and the result?

paragraphs.title: Menahem and His Dependence on Assyria

easy.explanation: Pul the king of Assyria came against the land.
easy.q: Who was the king of Assyria who came against the land?

easy.explanation: Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver.
easy.q: How much silver did Menahem give to Pul?

easy.explanation: Pekahiah his son reigned in Menahem’s stead.

answers: To strengthen his hold on the kingdom
To build the house of the LORD
medium.explanation: Menahem paid Pul so that Pul’s hand would be with him to confirm the kingdom.

answers: A unit of weight used for silver
medium.explanation: A talent was a unit of weight, and here it measured silver.
medium.q: What is a “talent” in this passage?

answers: The mighty men of wealth in Israel
medium.explanation: Menahem exacted the money from all the mighty men of wealth in Israel.
medium.q: From whom did Menahem collect the money given to the king of Assyria?

answers: The king of Assyria stayed in the land for many years
The king of Assyria turned back and did not stay in the land
Menahem was immediately removed from the throne
challenge.explanation: After receiving the money, the king of Assyria turned back and stayed not in the land.
challenge.q: What was the result of Menahem’s payment to Pul?

answers: Menahem did not know about Assyria
challenge.explanation: Menahem relied on Assyria and its king to confirm his rule.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Menahem’s need to pay Pul in order to secure his throne?

answers: Pekahiah reigned, Menahem paid, and Pul came
Pul came, Menahem paid him, and Pekahiah succeeded Menahem
Menahem died, Pul came, and then Menahem reigned
challenge.explanation: Pul came against the land, Menahem paid him, and Pekahiah later succeeded Menahem.

easy.explanation: Pekahiah reigned over Israel two years.
easy.q: How many years did Pekahiah reign?

easy.explanation: Pekah conspired against Pekahiah and killed him.
Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria carried the inhabitants captive to Assyria.
easy.q: Which power carried away the inhabitants of the northern territories?

answers: In the palace of the king’s house in Samaria
At the gate of the house of the LORD
medium.explanation: Pekah smote Pekahiah in Samaria, in the palace of the king’s house.

answers: Forcibly removed them from their land
medium.explanation: Assyria took the people away from their land by force.

answers: Assyria conquered northern areas and carried their inhabitants away
Israel and Judah became one kingdom
medium.explanation: Tiglath-pileser took several northern territories and carried their people captive.

answers: Both continued in the sins of Jeroboam
Both died peacefully in old age
challenge.explanation: The passage says of both kings that they departed not from the sins of Jeroboam.
challenge.q: What did Pekahiah and Pekah have in common?

challenge.explanation: Pekahiah reigned, Pekah killed him, and Hoshea later killed Pekah.
challenge.q: What was the order of rule in this passage?

answers: The northern people voluntarily moved to Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: Assyria conquered many northern territories and carried their inhabitants captive.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the conquest and captivity during Pekah’s reign?

paragraphs.title: Jotham’s Reign and the Threat to Judah

easy.explanation: Jotham the son of Uzziah reigned after Azariah.
easy.q: Who reigned in Judah after Azariah?

easy.explanation: Jotham reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
easy.q: How many years did Jotham reign in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: Jotham built the higher gate of the house of the LORD.
easy.q: What did Jotham build at the house of the LORD?

answers: He did what was right in the sight of the LORD
He did evil in the sight of the LORD
medium.explanation: Jotham did that which was right in the sight of the LORD.

answers: Places of worship where people sacrificed and burned incense
medium.explanation: The people continued to sacrifice and burn incense at the high places.
medium.q: What were the “high places” in this passage?

medium.explanation: The high places were not removed during Jotham’s reign.
medium.q: What remained despite Jotham’s good actions?

answers: Rezin and Pekah the son of Remaliah
challenge.explanation: The LORD began to send against Judah Rezin and Pekah during Jotham’s reign.
challenge.q: Who began to send enemies against Judah in the days of Jotham?

answers: Jotham succeeded Azariah, and Ahaz succeeded Jotham
challenge.explanation: Jotham reigned in Azariah’s stead, and Ahaz reigned in Jotham’s stead after his death.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the end and beginning of the passage?

answers: Judah continued building and governing during a time of military threat
The threat caused Jotham to stop ruling
challenge.explanation: Jotham built the higher gate while Rezin and Pekah began opposing Judah.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the temple construction occurring while enemies threatened Judah?
